intro.objective: Write ordinary numbers in standard form (A × 10ⁿ where 1 ≤ A < 10). Convert from standard form to ordinary numbers. Understand when n is positive (large numbers) and when n is negative (small numbers).
commonMistakes: A must be between 1 and 10 (1 ≤ A < 10). Writing 36 × 10⁴ is NOT standard form — it should be 3.6 × 10⁵.
Confusing the sign of the power — positive power = large number, negative power = small number.
Counting the wrong number of places when moving the decimal point.
methodSteps: Step 1: Identify A — move the decimal so there is one non-zero digit before it (1 ≤ A < 10).
Step 2: Count how many places the decimal moved — this is the power n.
Step 3: If the original number is ≥ 1, n is POSITIVE.
Step 4: If the original number is < 1, n is NEGATIVE.
Step 5: Write as A × 10ⁿ. Check: multiply back to verify.
workedExample: Step 1 — Move decimal to get 4.7 (one non-zero digit before the point).
Step 2 — The decimal moved 4 places to the right.
Step 3 — Original is less than 1, so n is negative.

questions.content:
Write in standard form:

   a) 5,000       b) 340,000       c) 72,000,000       d) 810

Write in standard form:

   a) 0.003       b) 0.00056       c) 0.0000012       d) 0.47

Convert to ordinary numbers:

   a) 3.2 × 10⁴       b) 7.05 × 10⁶       c) 1.8 × 10⁻³       d) 9.1 × 10⁻⁵

Which of these are NOT in correct standard form? Fix the ones that are wrong.

   a) 5.6 × 10³       b) 36 × 10⁴       c) 0.8 × 10⁻²       d) 7 × 10⁹

The mass of a hydrogen atom is about 0.000 000 000 000 000 000 000 001 67 kg.

Write this in standard form.

The distance from the Earth to the Sun is approximately 1.5 × 10⁸ km.

   a) Write this as an ordinary number.
   b) The distance to Mars is about 2.3 × 10⁸ km. Which planet is closer?
   c) How much further is Mars than the Sun? Give your answer in standard form.

Put in order, smallest first:

   3.2 × 10⁻³       8.1 × 10⁻⁴       5.5 × 10⁻³       2.9 × 10⁻²

Explain your strategy.

A bacterium is 2 × 10⁻⁶ m long. A virus is 3 × 10⁻⁸ m long.

   a) How many times longer is the bacterium than the virus? (2 marks)
   b) 500 bacteria placed end to end. Total length in standard form? (1 mark)
   c) How many viruses side by side fit in 1 mm? Give in standard form. (2 marks)
